scope: Complete author reading of all twenty-eight AI Mode pages and all five Studio pages, compared with provider, adapter, runtime, planner, query, patch, context, MCP, Studio router/settings/CLI and static-UI source plus existing scoped execution evidence. This does not certify provider quality, network reachability, browser interaction, autonomous workflows, production Studio exposure or final candidate behavior.

reviews.reason: Separates experimental provider and development helpers from the stable synchronous MCP boundary and routes readers to concrete entry points.
Uses global settings, current AI Hub commands and actual per-call limit objects while excluding durable provider state and a nonexistent AgentRuntime.
Distinguishes current, compatibility and deprecated provider layers, lists implementation-read environment names and discloses heuristic detection false positive and false negative behavior.
Keeps external provider adapters and illustrative client code outside the stable backend contract; live SDK and provider behavior remain application-tested responsibilities.
Uses OLLAMA_BASE_URL and OLLAMA_MODEL, matches the installed adapter entry points and warns that detection is not reachability.
Uses the environment names and adapter defaults actually loaded, explains dotted response paths and bounds compatibility to explicitly configured endpoint protocols.
Describes the existing CLI, Studio endpoints and provider workflow while treating compatibility detection as a hint rather than connectivity proof.
Documents exported connector adapters and their separate environment contract without treating generated text or connector metadata as authorization.
The provider-free greeting is installed-wheel verified and the page distinguishes local routing from provider execution, persistence and application authority.
Separates deterministic prompt-pack construction from optional provider execution and lists existing CLI and Studio endpoints as experimental.
Uses the actual ordered development-workflow structures and limits without presenting them as Durable Operations or a persistent workflow engine.
Replaces a nonexistent AgentRuntime with real process-local tracking and bounded-execution primitives and keeps durable execution separate.
Describes project-context and playbook prompt assembly as read-only development output, with CLI entry points and no autonomous-session claim.
Matches run_prompt_pack dispatch and limit inputs while excluding provider quality, durable counters and agent orchestration.
Documents structured plan validation and registered handler execution rather than LLM planning, persistence or autonomous goal selection.
Presents the rule-based read-only analyzer, score categories and existing CLI/Studio paths as experimental review output.
Uses actual structured code-generation models, leaves output unwritten and requires review, migrations, tests and source control.
Uses declarative preview/apply functions and explicit confirmation while bounding validation as a damage-reduction layer rather than autonomous maintenance.
Matches the in-process graph, bounded event timeline, five-second cache, context builders and existing Studio/CLI integrations, all labeled experimental.
Uses a structured query plan, discloses fetch-before-slice behavior and requires application authorization and tenancy before this low-level helper.
Describes the heuristic read-only analyzer, fixed thresholds, score model and existing CLI/Studio paths without promising measured application performance.
Uses actual context builders and distinguishes ai_sensitive filtering from permission, policy, tenant and RLS enforcement.
Places stable MCP, experimental code helpers, process-local state and Durable Operations on separate authority and lifetime boundaries.
The executable decorator example and installed CLI forms match metadata-only behavior and explicitly deny authorization or approval semantics.
Separates discovered synchronous MCP tools from JSON inspection and experimental development helpers, including custom-handler authorization ownership.
Uses the installed schema-health/schema-issues commands and analyzer import, and keeps analysis distinct from migrations and production Doctor.
Explains the stable synchronous protocol boundary, current authorization, approval, audit and limits while excluding protocol MCP Tasks and durable sessions.
Keeps heuristic analysis and suggestions read-only, process-local and outside provider or production-monitoring guarantees.
Keeps Studio opt-in and experimental, provides a loopback quickstart and describes selected live process state without claiming complete backend visibility.
Matches enablement, production exposure, required secret, Origin, bearer and staff-session behavior while warning that Studio access is not record authorization.
Reframes the page as selected core endpoints, states authentication independently from Origin and identifies capability metadata as conditional and descriptive.
Installed help confirms the five Studio commands; samples use v0.7.0 and URL formatting is no longer described as a mount or reachability check.
Uses the v0.7 experimental boundary, requires a live backend, gives complete production mount prerequisites and distinguishes browser staff cookies from API bearer clients.

execution_evidence: studio access dependency cases in installed-doc-imports.json

functional_findings.boundary: The experimental compatibility provider detector reports default Ollama as configured without environment or reachability, and rejects a keyless custom endpoint even though the adapter accepts one.
